what_its_for: Clomipramine is used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). This means it helps reduce unwanted, repeated thoughts (obsessions) and the urge to repeat certain behaviors (compulsions) that interfere with your daily life. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other conditions.
how_to_take: Take clomipramine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. It is best to take it with food or milk to help prevent stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time(s) every day to keep a steady level in your body. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks. A typical starting dose for adults is 25 mg per day. The dose is usually increased gradually up to 100–250 mg per day. Your doctor will find the dose that works best for you. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms like nausea, headache, or dizziness.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store clomipramine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about a local medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking clomipramine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid standing up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can lower your blood pressure and cause dizziness. Do not take other medicines — including over-the-counter drugs, herbal supplements, or other antidepressants — without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist. Especially avoid MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine or selegiline), as combining them with clomipramine can be life-threatening. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to the sun; use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or others, unusual or sudden changes in mood or behavior, seizures, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, difficulty urinating, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), fever with stiff muscles and confusion (signs of a serious reaction called serotonin syndrome), or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also let your doctor know about any new or worsening symptoms, including increased anxiety, agitation, or restlessness, especially in the first few weeks of treatment. In the US, you can also contact the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 to report side effects.
when_it_works: Clomipramine does not work right away. It may take 2 to 4 weeks before you start to notice any improvement in your symptoms, and it may take up to 8 to 12 weeks to feel the full benefit. It is very important to keep taking the medicine every day, even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Children and teenagers: Clomipramine can be used in children age 10 and older for OCD, but children and teens should be watched closely for any changes in mood, behavior, or thoughts of self-harm, especially in the first few months of treatment. Older adults (65+): Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, confusion, and falls. A lower starting dose is often recommended. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may pose risks to an unborn baby or nursing infant, and your doctor will help weigh the risks and benefits for you. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, tell your doctor before starting this medicine, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
